messages.subject: Re: Doubt regarding estimation of standard error
messages.subject_clean: Doubt regarding estimation of standard error
messages.body_plain:
You never want complete, it is the information matrix matrix from the complete data solution (which is overly conservative, because it assumes you know the values of theta...which you don't). You probably want 'Louis' instead, which should be more accurate since its the actual observed information matrix (the crossprod is an approximation to this, but its very cheap to compute).

That being said, good luck getting a positive definite information matrix for the 3PL model, You sample size must be *very* large for this to occur, which is one of the downsides of this model. Cheers.

Phil

First off, let me just say you've done an amazing job with this R package, and a lot of us grad students (and professionals) are thrilled to be able to use it.

Okay, my question: I'm not able to find standard errors with createItem(). It keeps kicking back the error below:

Error in Estep.mirt(pars = pars[[g]], tabdata = gtabdata, freq = 1L, CUSTOM.IND = CUSTOM.IND,  :
  argument "full" is missing, with no default

name <- 'old2PL'
par <- c(a = .5, b = -2)
est <- c(TRUE, TRUE)
P.old2PL <- function(par,Theta, ncat){
        a <- par[1]
        b <- par[2]
        P1 <- 1 / (1 + exp(-1*a*(Theta - b)))
        cbind(1-P1, P1)
}

x <- createItem(name, par=par, est=est, P=P.old2PL)
#So, let's estimate it!
dat <- expand.table(LSAT7)
sv <- mirt(dat, 1, c(rep('2PL',4), 'old2PL'), customItems=list(old2PL=x), pars = 'values')
tail(sv) #looks good
mod <- mirt(dat, 1, c(rep('2PL',4), 'old2PL'), SE.type='Fisher',SE=TRUE, customItems=list(old2PL=x))
coef(mod, printSE=TRUE)

Note that I added the SE.type='Fisher', SE=TRUE and the printSE=TRUE. The rest is straight from your documentation.

Can you explain a little about what the function is doing, and why it can't find standard errors? I'm looking forward to hearing from you.
Thanks
Charlie

Phil

Chris

change starting values
use different method, especially MH-RM

Chris

Currently, I can't suggest much that stays directly within the IRT framework. It is possible to extend the M2 statistic to create a hybrid-type model for polytomous data to fix this problem, but I haven't had the time to invest in such an endeavour.

You may have luck switching to the SEM framework with lavaan if your items are ordered (2PL and graded), and estimate the items as ordinal, but even then I'm not convinced the problem will be solved (it's very likely that the bivariate tables will be sparse and will cause difficulties).

Phil

messages.body_plain:
I don't really see the need for it. Item EFA can be done in mirt, and things like missing data are dealt with much better, detecting mis-fitting items, overall model fit, computing factor scores, and so on. Not to mention, it might actually be faster to do FIML estimation than limited information methods in R if the number of items is large. Plus, irt.fa seems to only support dichotomous items that have to have a 2PLM form, whereas mirt can work with a mix of dichotomous/polytomous types and with items other than the 2PL.

But that's just my 2 cents, use whatever works best for your data.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Question about the function of "iteminfo"
messages.body_plain:
You're not technically wrong, information functions are definitely better defined in unidimensional models, but you can still get at their essence with a method that Mark Reckase has discussed (section 5.2 of his MIRT book, or see Reckase and Mckinley, 1991). Essentially, you need to specify a viewing angle to collapse the multiple dimensions to a single dimension by applying a directional derivative. So that can be done like so:

library(mirt)
mod <- mirt(Science, 2)
extr.2 <- extract.item(mod, 2)
Theta <- matrix(seq(-4,4, by = .1))
Theta2 <- as.matrix(expand.grid(Theta, Theta))
info.2 <- iteminfo(extr.2, Theta2, degrees = c(45,45))
head(data.frame(Theta2, info=info.2))

I would only use these for plots though as they really don't include the covariance between the traits for other numerical routines (the package actually does only use these for plotting).

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Question about the function of "iteminfo"
messages.body_plain:
Could you clarify how to specify the angle? The documentation says that it should be a vector of degrees summing to 90. This seems correct for two-dimensional models (per Reckase's MIRT book, the constraint is that the cosines of the angles need to sum to 1). For higher dimensional models, it doesn't seem right, though. If I want to plot the information parallel to Dimension 1 in a three-dimensional model, shouldn't the vector of angles be c(0, 90, 90)? Am I misunderstanding how the function works?

(On a side note, the itemplot(..., type="info", degrees=c() ) function seems to work a bit counter-intuintuitively. When there are 3 or more dimensions, one specifies a vector of angles with length equal to the number of dimensions, which is passed to the iteminfo function. For 2-dimensional models, however, the function concatenates the supplied vector with an additional value (presumably to allow specifying just 1 angle, which is easier). If one supplies a vector of length 2 (i.e., gives both angles), then the function still appends the additional angle to the vector, which changes the results (and seems to be incorrect). )

Thanks,
Brenton

> library(mirt)

> extr.2 <- extract.item(mod, 2)
> Theta <- matrix(seq(-4,4, by = .1))
> Theta2 <- as.matrix(expand.grid(Theta, Theta))
> info.2 <- iteminfo(extr.2, Theta2, degrees = c(45,45))
> head(data.frame(Theta2, info=info.2))
>
> I would only use these for plots though as they really don't include the covariance between the traits for other numerical routines (the package actually does only use these for plotting).
>
> Phil
